keywords: The Petitioner claims that his uncle (3rd Respondent) failed to succeed to the rights as a successor of his late grandfather, who had been the original grantee of a parcel of land given under the Land Development Ordinance. However, the Respondents’ stand is that the 3rd Respondent could not have succeeded after the death of the original grantee in 1996 until the death of the spouse of the original grantee (mother of the 3rd Respondent) in terms of Section 48B. The question of succession arose thereafter in 2022, and the 3rd Respondent has duly applied to register his succession which had been nominated by the original grantee under the original permit issued prior to the grant. Held – acceptance of the 3rd Respondent as the successor by the Divisional Secretary on the instructions of the Commissioner General of Land is valid, and therefore, the registration in the Land Registry of the 3rd Respondent as the successor to the original grantee is valid; Application dismissed.

keywords: The Petitioner, a Society running a religious institute and Hindu Temple, was occupying a land within the vicinity of the Sri Maha Bodhi in the sacred city of Anuradhapura. Later, with the dawn of the Buddha Jayanthi era of 1956, the Petitioner was relocated by giving a land, where the Petitioner also ran a school which was vested in the Government under the Assisted Schools and Training Colleges Act. Thereafter, the Petitioner was placed in possession of another land, where it operated a religious institute including a Temple, cultural centre, and restaurant. The excess land was blocked out and given to the 8th to 10th Respondents. Dispute arose between them with regard to the regularisation and legalisation of their possession by the Government on the recommendation of the Provincial Land Commissioner, which the Petitioner objected to. Held - Application dismissed on the basis that the Petitioner has no legal title to claim nor any legitimate expectation to claim any title document since the Petitioner has failed to improve or develop the entire land; the Petitioner is not entitled to benefit out of his own fault.

judgement_by: Ho.n.Dr. D. F. H. Gunawardhana, J.
keywords: The Petitioner was involved in two robberies while serving as a police officer. Though he was acquitted from criminal proceedings, he was charge-sheeted by a disciplinary panel appointed by the Senior DIG of the range to which he was attached. Panel of Inquiry found him guilty on the strong evidence against him; findings against him by the Panel of Inquiry was further affirmed by the Public Service Commission and Administrative Appeal Tribunal. However, on sympathetic grounds he was permitted to retire. The Petitioner challenges the vires of the appointment of Panel of Inquiry and its findings. Held – the Petitioner, being a Sub- Inspector, is subject to the disciplinary control of the Senior DIG of the range to which he is attached, therefore, the appointment is intra vires and based on the facts, the final findings of the AAT is justified; thus, Application dismissed.
legistation: The Constitution of the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka

keywords: The Petitioner had filed an application to obtain a Faskh divorce before the Quazi Court of Gampaha. However, later having withdrawn that application, she had changed her residence to Panadura, where she had instituted a similar application. The Respondent had raised objections to the maintainability because she had recently come to reside within the jurisdiction of the Panadura Quazi Court; objection overruled, and proceeded with the divorce. Later, the Respondent, without notice, obtained a stay order from the Board of Quazi, and thereafter notified the Petitioner. Since there is a procedural error made by the Board of Quazi by not hearing the Petitioner, Court granted relief as prayed for

keywords: The Petitioner being the eldest child of the original permit holder, who had died and nominated his wife as the successor, sought to be substituted. The same permit holder held two plots of land, one on permit issued under the Land Development Ordinance, and the other one’s permit was on the pipeline to be issued. The widow never made an application to succeed within the time stipulated as she had also died within sixteen months of the death of the original permit holder. The Divisional Secretary decided to amalgamate both lands and divided into equal shares among all the children. The Petitioner successfully invoked the jurisdiction of this Court to obtain a Writ of Certiorari and Mandamus to declare him as the successor in respect of the plot of land held under permit.

description: Neshakumaran Vimalaraj Vs The University Grants Commission and Others before Hon.Dr. D. F. H. Gunawardhana, J.
parties: Neshakumaran Vimalaraj Vs The University Grants Commission and Others
judgement_by: Hon.Dr. D. F. H. Gunawardhana, J.
keywords: The Petitioner was a Council Member of the Eastern University for a period of three years. After the present Government came into power, the members of the University Grants Commission were newly appointed and they requested the Petitioner to resign from his said post; on refusal, he was removed. The said decision was challenged by way of writ. The main defense taken up by the Respondents was that the Petitioner was removed in implementing National policy. However, the National policy that was relied upon was the election manifesto of a political party. Held – no election manifesto can be accepted or adopted as National policy if it is violative of the law and Constitution, unless the law and Constitution are changed. Writ of Certiorari and Mandamus was issued.
legistation: The Constitution of the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka

keywords: The Petitioner being the eldest child of the original permit holder, who had died and nominated his wife as the successor, sought to be substituted. The same permit holder held two plots of land, one on permit issued under the Land Development Ordinance, and the other one’s permit was on the pipeline to be issued. The widow never made an application to succeed within the time stipulated as she had also died within sixteen months of the death of the original permit holder. The Divisional Secretary decided to amalgamate both lands and divided into equal shares among all the children. The Petitioner successfully invoked the jurisdiction of this Court to obtain a Writ of Certiorari and Mandamus to declare him as the successor in respect of the plot of land held under permit.

description: Neshakumaran Vimalaraj Vs The University Grants Commission and Others before Hon.Dr. D. F. H. Gunawardhana, J.
parties: Neshakumaran Vimalaraj Vs The University Grants Commission and Others
judgement_by: Hon.Dr. D. F. H. Gunawardhana, J.
keywords: The Petitioner was a Council Member of the Eastern University for a period of three years. After the present Government came into power, the members of the University Grants Commission were newly appointed and they requested the Petitioner to resign from his said post; on refusal, he was removed. The said decision was challenged by way of writ. The main defense taken up by the Respondents was that the Petitioner was removed in implementing National policy. However, the National policy that was relied upon was the election manifesto of a political party. Held – no election manifesto can be accepted or adopted as National policy if it is violative of the law and Constitution, unless the law and Constitution are changed. Writ of Certiorari and Mandamus was issued.
legistation: The Constitution of the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka

keywords: Partition action instituted in the District Court of Tangalle in respect of land situated within the same jurisdiction. Allegations that the entire land has not been depicted in the preliminary plan. However, before the commencement of the trial, the Petitioner sought the intervention of the writ court to obtain a writ compelling the District Court Judge to dismiss the action for the want of proper identification of the corpus. Held – the writ court cannot intervene into the matter since it affects the Judicial power of the parties since only the District Court of Tangalle has the jurisdiction in terms of Section 3(2) of the Partition Law, Section 6 of the Civil Procedure Code, and the Constitution. Though the writ court is empowered to issue writs, when there is no allegation of irrationality, act of ultra vires affecting the rights of the parties, or acted without evidence, no writ lies.
legistation: The Constitution of the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka

keywords: Two different decision of the Supreme Court on the Rule 49 (xii)(a) - In one judgement holds that the Rule is ultra vires and in the other its intra vires– In the former it is obiter dictum and the later it is ratiodecidendi – Doctrine of stare decisis – The test to be applied in deciding whether it is obiter dictum or ratio decidendi–The words ‘appears to be’ used in the judgement- No certainty in the mind of the judge – Not a definitive finding – re-arguing the same issue in courts repeatedly – Unproductive practice – Has to be discouraged – the learned High Court Judge failed to address the other issue raised by the Petition – Part of the judgement affirm but set a side the judgement dismissing the writ application in its entirely - case remitted back to the high Court to make a determination on the other issue.
